name: The Dhammapada
translation: Pali Canon — Max Müller & Buddhist Publication Society

chapters.name: Yamaka-vagga (The Twin Verses)
chapters.subtitle: On the nature of thought, speech, and consequence

verses.text: Mind precedes all mental states. Mind is their chief; they are all mind-wrought. If with an impure mind a person speaks or acts, suffering follows him like the wheel that follows the foot of the ox.
verses.original: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā manosseṭṭhā manomayā, manasā ce paduṭṭhena bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṁ dukkhamanveti cakkaṁva vahato padaṁ.

verses.text: Mind precedes all mental states. Mind is their chief; they are all mind-wrought. If with a pure mind a person speaks or acts, happiness follows him like his never-departing shadow.
verses.original: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā manosseṭṭhā manomayā, manasā ce pasannena bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṁ sukhamanveti chāyāva anapāyinī.

verses.text: ‘He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me’ — in those who harbor such thoughts, hatred is not appeased.
verses.original: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ ajini maṁ ahāsi me, ye ca taṁ upanayhanti veraṁ tesaṁ na sammati.

verses.text: ‘He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me’ — in those who do not harbor such thoughts, hatred is appeased.
verses.original: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ ajini maṁ ahāsi me, ye ca taṁ nupanayhanti veraṁ tesūpasammati.

verses.text: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased. This is an eternal truth.
verses.original: Na hi verena verāni sammantīdha kudācanaṁ, averena ca sammanti esa dhammo sanantano.
verses.transliteration: Na hi verena verāni sammantīdha kudācanaṁ...

verses.text: There are those who do not realize that one day we all must die. But those who do realize this settle their quarrels at once.
verses.original: Pare ca na vijānanti mayamettha yamāmase, ye ca tattha vijānanti tato sammanti medhagā.

verses.text: Heedfulness is the path to the Deathless (Nibbana); heedlessness is the path to death. The heedful do not die; the heedless are like unto the dead already.
verses.original: Appamādo amatapadaṁ pamādo maccuno padaṁ, appamattā na mīyanti ye pamattā yathā matā.

verses.text: Clearly understanding this excellence of heedfulness, the wise rejoice in heedfulness, delighting in the realm of the Noble Ones.
verses.original: Evaṁ visesato ñatvā appamādamhi paṇḍitā, appamāde pamodanti ariyānaṁ gocare ratā.

verses.text: These wise ones, meditative, persevering, always using strong effort, attain Nibbana, the unsurpassed freedom from bondage.
verses.original: Te jhāyino sātatikā niccaṁ daḷhaparakkamā, phusanti dhīrā nibbānaṁ yogakkhemaṁ anuttaraṁ.

verses.text: Whoever is energetic, mindful, pure in conduct, discerning, self-restrained, righteous in living, and heedful — his glory grows.
verses.original: Uṭṭhānavato satimato sucikammassa nisammakārino, saññatassa ca dhammajīvino appamattassa yasobhivaḍḍhati.

chapters.name: Citta-vagga (The Mind)
chapters.subtitle: On guarding and mastering the restless mind

verses.text: Just as a fletcher straightens an arrow, so the discerning person straightens the mind, which is fickle, wavering, difficult to guard and difficult to control.
verses.original: Phandanaṁ capalaṁ cittaṁ durakkhaṁ dunnivārayaṁ, ujuṁ karoti medhāvī usukārova tejanaṁ.

verses.text: Like a fish pulled from its watery home and cast on dry ground, this mind thrashes about trying to escape the realm of Mara.
verses.original: Vārijova thale khitto okamokataubbhuto, pariphandatidaṁ cittaṁ māradheyyaṁ pahātave.

verses.text: Hard to restrain, swift, flying wherever it pleases is the mind. To master such a mind is good; a controlled mind brings true happiness.
verses.original: Dunniggahassa lahuno yatthakāmanipātino, cittassa damatho sādhu cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.

verses.text: Whatever a hater may do to a hater, or an enemy to an enemy, a wrongly directed mind does oneself far greater harm.
verses.original: Diso disaṁ yaṁ taṁ kayirā verī vā pana verinaṁ, micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ pāpiyo naṁ tato kare.

verses.text: Neither father nor mother, nor any other relative can do as much good as a well-directed mind.
verses.original: Na taṁ mātā pitā kayirā aññe vāpi ca ñātakā, sammāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ seyyaso naṁ tato kare.

chapters.name: Puppha-vagga (Flowers)
chapters.subtitle: On gathering the fragrant flowers of virtue

verses.text: The scent of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor that of sandalwood, tagara, or jasmine. But the fragrance of the virtuous travels against the wind; the virtuous person pervades all directions.
verses.original: Na pupphagandho paṭivātameti na candanaṁ tagaramallikā vā, satañca gandho paṭivātameti sabbā disā sappuriso pavāyati.

verses.text: Just as from a heap of flowers many garlands can be made, so by a mortal once born many good deeds should be done.
verses.original: Yathāpi puppharāsimhā kayirā mālāguṇe bahū, evaṁ jātena maccena kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ bahuṁ.

verses.text: Long is the night to the sleepless; long is the league to the weary traveler; long is the round of rebirth (samsara) to the foolish who know not the sublime truth.
verses.original: Dīghā jāgarato ratti dīghaṁ santassa yojanaṁ, dīgho bālānaṁ saṁsāro saddhammaṁ avijānataṁ.

verses.text: If a traveler does not meet a companion who is better or equal, let him firmly pursue a solitary course; there is no fellowship with a fool.
verses.original: Carañce nādhigaccheyya seyyaṁ sadisamattano, ekacariyaṁ daḷhaṁ kayirā natthi bāle sahāyatā.

verses.text: A fool who knows his foolishness is wise at least to that extent. But a fool who thinks he is wise is called a fool indeed.
verses.original: Yo bālo maññati bālyaṁ paṇḍito vāpi tena so, bālo ca paṇḍitamānī sa ve bāloti vuccati.

verses.text: Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, even so the wise are not moved by praise or blame.
verses.original: Selo yathā ekaghano vātena na samīrati, evaṁ nindāpasaṁsāsu na samiñjanti paṇḍitā.

verses.text: Even as a deep, still lake is clear and calm, so the wise become tranquil after listening to the Dhamma.
verses.original: Yathāpi rahado gambhīro vippasanno anāvilo, evaṁ dhammāni sutvāna vippasīdanti paṇḍitā.

chapters.name: Arahanta-vagga (The Liberated)
chapters.subtitle: On the joy of freedom from craving

verses.text: For him who has completed his journey, who is free from sorrow, liberated in every way, and has shed all bonds — no fever of passion exists.
verses.original: Gataddhino visokassa vippamuttassa sabbadhi, sabbaganthappahīnassa pariḷāho na vijjati.

verses.text: Calm is his mind, calm is his speech, and calm is his action who, through right knowledge, is wholly freed and at peace.
verses.original: Santaṁ tassa manaṁ hoti santā vācā ca kamma ca, sammadaññā vimuttassa upasantassa tādino.

chapters.name: Sahassa-vagga (The Thousands)
chapters.subtitle: On the supreme value of one word of peace

verses.text: Better than a thousand useless words is one single meaningful word, upon hearing which one attains peace.
verses.original: Sahassamapi ce vācā anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ atthapadaṁ seyyo yaṁ sutvā upasammati.

verses.text: Though one may conquer in battle a thousand times a thousand men, yet he who conquers himself alone is the greatest of conquerors.
verses.original: Yo sahassaṁ sahassena saṅgāme mānuse jine, ekañca jeyyamattānaṁ sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo.

verses.text: One truly is the protector of oneself; who else could the protector be? With oneself thoroughly tamed, one discovers a refuge that is hard to gain.
verses.original: Attā hi attano nātho ko hi nātho paro siyā, attanā hi sudantena nāthaṁ labhati dullabhaṁ.

verses.text: By oneself alone is evil done; by oneself is one defiled. By oneself is evil left undone; by oneself is one purified. Purity and impurity depend on oneself; no one can purify another.
verses.original: Attanā hi kataṁ pāpaṁ attanā saṅkilissati, attanā akataṁ pāpaṁ attanāva visujjhati, suddhī asuddhī paccattaṁ nāñño aññaṁ visodhaye.

chapters.name: Magga-vagga (The Path)
chapters.subtitle: The Noble Eightfold Path to liberation

verses.text: Of paths the Eightfold is the best; of truths the Four Sayings are the best; of virtues detachment is the best; and of men the Seer (the Buddha) is the best.
verses.original: Maggānaṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho saccānaṁ caturo padā, virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṁ dvipadānañca cakkhumā.

verses.text: This is the only path; there is no other that leads to the purification of insight. Follow this path, and you will confound Mara (illusion).
verses.original: Esove maggo natthañño dassanassa visuddhiyā, etaṁhi tumhe paṭipajjatha mārassetaṁ pamohanaṁ.

verses.text: You yourselves must strive; the Buddhas only show the way. Those who enter the path and practice meditation are freed from the bonds of death.
verses.original: Tumhehi kiccamātappaṁ akkhātāro tathāgatā, paṭipannā pamokkhanti jhāyino mārabandhanā.
